title: The spatial impact assessment of landfill sites on air quality in Surabaya: a diurnal and seasonal perspective
content: Air quality is a critical determinant of human and environmental health, and residents living near municipal waste disposal sites may be exposed to elevated particulate concentrations. This study characterised air quality adjacent to the Benowo landfill in Surabaya, Indonesia, using an automated monitoring station that recorded PM1, PM2.5, PM10, CO2, temperature and humidity at 15-minute intervals between 3 April 2020 and 31 December 2024. PM2.5 and PM10 span the whole record; CO2 began in 2021, and PM1, temperature and humidity began in 2022, so the analyses involving these variables cover shorter periods. A total of 143 330 valid PM2.5 observations were analysed. Annual mean PM2.5 increased from 37.17 µg m−3 in 2020 to 50.32 µg m−3 in 2024, exceeding the WHO annual guideline by 7–10 times, and the trend is significant (r = 0.970 and p = 0.006). The mean US AQI rose from 101.28 to 125.25 over the same period. Night-time concentrations (18:00–05:59) exceeded daytime concentrations (06:00–17:59), with means of 44.56 ± 48.08 and 41.26 ± 77.36 µg m−3, medians of 37.0 and 29.0 µg m−3, and WHO guideline exceedance rates of 51.7% and 40.4% respectively. The highest monthly exceedance rates occurred in November (58.2%), April (56.0%) and June (53.7%), the highest hourly rate was 75.9% at 07:00, and exceedance rates of weekdays exceeded those of weekends, with Tuesday (49.0%) and Wednesday (47.8%) showing the highest rates. The transition seasons (April–May and October–November) showed the highest seasonal exceedance rate (52.1%), higher than those of the cold dry season (47.7%) and the hot wet season (36.2%). Temperature and humidity were strongly negatively correlated (r = −0.87), whereas the association between temperature and PM2.5 was weak (r = −0.038); the mean temperature during the highest 5% of PM2.5 concentrations was nevertheless lower than the overall mean (28.3 °C against 29.6 °C), indicating that cooler, more stable conditions accompany the most severe episodes. Because the monitoring design records total mass at a single site without chemical speciation, the contribution of the landfill cannot be separated from those of traffic, industry and regional biomass burning. The results indicate sustained exposure above health-based thresholds across diurnal, weekly and seasonal scales and support targeted mitigation at the site and along the adjacent traffic corridors.
